console.title: GemArc MCP · Feature Tuning Console
console.foot.note: The console only calls the MCP tools this server really registers; it simulates nothing.
console.filter.placeholder: Filter by tool name or description…
console.tool.hint: Every item on the left is a tool really registered in the MCP protocol. Select one to adjust its parameters and call it.
console.result.empty: The result of a call appears here. An error is shown as the raw JSON-RPC error, without embellishment.
console.result.ready: The parameters are ready; press Call to run.
console.result.copydenied: The browser refused clipboard access; copy it by hand
console.err.token401: The token is invalid or was rotated (HTTP 401). Paste the token again above.
console.err.session401: The sign-in session is invalid or expired (HTTP 401). Sign in again, or paste a token on the right.
console.err.needtoken401: This server needs an access token (HTTP 401). Paste one above.
console.err.notjson: The server did not return JSON (HTTP {status})
console.err.badjson: The parameter {name} is not valid JSON: {message}
console.auth.label: MCP access token
console.auth.placeholder: Paste a Bearer token (kept only in this tab's sessionStorage)
console.auth.source: Tokens are issued on the account page
console.auth.sourcenote: The website (the account page) issues the token. Paste it here, or straight into your agent's configuration.
console.auth.sessionnote: Using the token saved in this tab (the sign-in session works too).
console.auth.sessionalt: Using the sign-in session; paste a token to act as someone else.
console.auth.tokensaved: Using the token saved in this tab.
console.auth.needtokenpaste: This server needs an access token; paste one and press Use token.
console.auth.badchars: The token contains invisible or non-ASCII characters (a zero-width space or a curly quote picked up while copying). Copy it again.
console.auth.cleared: The token in this tab is cleared.

accounts.lang.label: Language
accounts.signedout.note: The first successful sign-in is the registration. After that you can create personal access tokens for Claude Code, Codex and Hermes to call MCP.
accounts.privacy.login: Sign-in uses your Google account (only the openid and email scopes; no name, no avatar).
accounts.privacy.what: What is stored: your e-mail address and your Google account identifier, encrypted field by field in the database. No password and no Google token is ever stored.
accounts.privacy.why: Why it is stored: to recognise your account, to issue and revoke personal access tokens, and to keep the smallest possible security audit trail.
accounts.privacy.howlong: How long it is kept: as long as the account exists. Audit records are cleaned up after the days the operator sets. Deleting the account deletes the account data from the database (the provider's backups may still hold old data inside their retention window).
accounts.privacy.rights: Your rights: once you are signed in you can export all your data or delete your account at any time.
accounts.error.title: Something went wrong
accounts.error.email: The e-mail address you signed in with is {email}. If you believe you should be allowed, send that address to the operator.
accounts.deleted.title: Account deleted
accounts.deleted.body: Your account, sessions and tokens have been deleted from the database. The audit records are anonymised. The provider's backups may still hold old data inside their retention window.
accounts.deleted.revoke: You can also remove this application's access in your own Google account settings.
accounts.account.stale: For safety, creating tokens, revoking all of them, exporting and deleting need a sign-in within the last 15 minutes.
accounts.account.tokennewnote: Copy it and keep it safe now. It cannot be shown again after you leave this page; if you lose it, revoke it and create another one.
accounts.account.snipintro: You can also put the token into the environment variable GEMARC_MCP_PAT first; then the configuration file names the variable and never the token itself.
accounts.account.snipfilledh2: Configuration with the token already filled in
accounts.account.snipfillednote: The three configurations below are ready to copy into your agent: Claude Code and Hermes carry the token itself, and Codex points at GEMARC_MCP_PAT (that line is filled in below).
accounts.account.snipservice: Service address: {url}. The custom connector of claude.ai cannot use a token like this.
accounts.account.deletewarn: This permanently deletes the account {email}, its sessions and its tokens, and cannot be undone.
accounts.admin.allowedemails: E-mail addresses allowed to sign in
accounts.admin.siterebuildnote: A rebuild only clears the site this instance has materialised; the next visit to the site path builds it again. Other instances are not affected.
accounts.admin.settingsnote: An empty item is decided by the environment. The token policy takes effect at once; the tool set takes effect after the next cold start (a new deployment or a recycled instance).
